title: an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver
intention: Every component that receives a request it cannot fill raises a trouble at its own address, counted on every repeat, so a caller that keeps sending what cannot be done becomes visible and gets stopped.
why: Ruling 8h, 2026-10-05, Akien verbatim: "Any component that gets a request that it can't fill, that's a trouble ticket. We will eventually class certain classes of trouble is not requiring a ticket. Because like if we throw a trouble ticket because I mistype something on the Cairn command line, that might not be a trouble that I actually need to go look at.  But every requester that gets something they can't do should throw a ticket. Because we need to stop people throwing things at them that they can't do." The lived symptom: codemother asked inference_domain for a 'codemother' domain row that does not exist about 1,000 times a day, and every ask was refused in silence, so nobody could see the broken caller. This is spanning: every receiver implements it at its own boundary, so no one directory can hold it.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth): a refused request today is silent at the receiver. CP4 via Telos: the lived symptom is a component spending ~1000 refusals a day on a caller nobody can see. Ruling 8h, 2026-10-05.
how: One child per component boundary (RULE 1), each proved before this parent: the receiver's own refusal lane raises through raise_trouble (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py) with an identity naming what was asked, so the trouble device's fold on identity is the counter, and the detail names the caller. First child: e9a2d8ae7d43 at cairn/devices/inference_domain (an ask for a domain row that does not exist, the codemother case of ~1000/day). Then a declared refusal shape BaseShim recognizes, and a seam for the future no-ticket classes (a CLI typo), left empty. Which end raises (receiver only, both, or sender only per 7cb1989e7825's 2026-08-11 ruling) is a question bound to this ticket; the BaseShim bounce path waits for the answer. Finally the piece is written at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver.md quoting 8h verbatim and naming each child.
falsifier: GREEN when (a) each child's receiver raises exactly one trouble per unfillable request, the same identity on a repeat and a different one for a different ask, naming the caller; (b) the refusal the caller gets is unchanged, even when the trouble lane is down; (c) a fillable request raises nothing; (d) the which-end question is answered and the bounce path matches the answer. RED if any receiver refuses in silence or the trouble replaces the refusal. WRONG INTENT if the trouble lane floods with classes Akien never needs to look at (his CLI-typo case) before the no-ticket seam exists. Horizon: the codemother 'codemother' domain asks show as one counted trouble at inference_domain.
watchme: none, because the standing measurement is the trouble device's own fold count per identity at each receiver (e9a2d8ae7d43 raises inference-unfilled-domain-<name> into ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/), which the operator's trouble lane already shows
children: e9a2d8ae7d43 — cairn/devices/inference_domain: an ask for a domain row that does not exist raises one counted trouble at the receiver, naming the caller; the refusal is unchanged. FIRST.
a-declared-refusal-shape-baseshim-recognizes — cairn/tools/base: a handler's refusal travels in one declared shape the receiver's shim raises on; waits for the bound question.
a-seam-for-no-ticket-trouble-classes — the place a future class such as a cairn CLI typo is declared to need no ticket; left empty per 8h's FUTURE line.

decisions.text: D1: SETTLED: the children are proved first, one per component boundary (RULE 1), e9a2d8ae7d43 at cairn/devices/inference_domain first. Each child raises at its receiver through raise_trouble (cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py), with an identity naming what was asked (the fold on identity is the counter) and a detail naming the caller. The caller's refusal is unchanged.
D2: SETTLED: BaseShim's bounce path (handle_bounce, cairn/tools/base/shim.py:885) and the declared-refusal child wait for open-b9037ca75019. No change touches them until it is answered.
D3: SETTLED: the no-ticket seam is declared empty per 8h's FUTURE line. No class is exempted in this ticket.

D4: SETTLED: at BUILDME the piece is written at CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-an-unfillable-request-is-a-counted-trouble-at-the-receiver.md, quoting 8h verbatim and the answer to open-b9037ca75019 verbatim and naming each child's address. It is then compiled into the lab through cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh.
